newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ATHLETICS-KIPKETER BREAKS OLDEST RECORD IN BOOK.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KIPKETER BREAKS OLDEST RECORD IN BOOK.

text.p: Denmark's former Kenyan Wilson Kipketer broke the oldest world record in athletics on Wednesday when he smashed Seb Coe's 16-year-old mark for the men's 800 metres at the Zurich grand prix.

After equalling Coe's record of one minute 41.73 seconds in Stockholm earlier this season, Kipketer took advantage of a warm, still evening to clocked 1:41.24 and take the two-track race into new territory.

The world champion was just a youngster growing up in Kenya when Coe sped around a track in the Italian city of Florence to set the previous best in June 1981 with one of the most remarkable middle-distance performances of all time.

Helped through the first 400 metres in an astonishing 48.10 by compatriot Joseph Tengelei -- compared to Coe's 49.7 -- Kipketer stormed through the last 400 metres on his own and was roared on to the finish by an ecstatic Zurich crowd.
Twice last season, Kipketer, who went to live in Denmark in 1990, went close to the world record after missing the Atlanta Olympics because he was not cleared to run for his adopted country.

The Kenyan-born athlete earned a world record bonus of $50,000 for the Zurich performance plus one kilo of gold. With appearance money, Kipketer would have made at least $130,000 from the record-breaking run.
